statement: Non-smooth quantizers can incur regret H*Omega(1) even though in-distribution one-step error is only O(eps_q).
source: arXiv:2603.20538, Section 4.1 + appendix proof of Theorem 6 (deterministic-dynamic part)

prediction_P1_in_distribution_error.expected: O(eps_q) ~ 0.2200 (shrinks with eps_q); binning also O(eps_q)

mutation_test.name: replace non-smooth (learning-based) quantizer by binning (smooth) quantizer
mutation_test.effect: Binning removes the trap: deployment regret per step drops from Omega(1) (0.530) to O(eps_q) (0.03421); in-distribution error also O(eps_q). The H*Omega(1) failure disappears -> attributable to NON-SMOOTHNESS.

notes: Verified = the paper's exact trap-loop construction reproduces both predictions: IN-DISTRIBUTION one-step error is O(eps_q) (0.2188) while DEPLOYMENT regret is H*Omega(1) (per-step ~0.530, essentially independent of eps_q; see vs_eps_q). The binning-quantizer mutation removes the trap and reduces regret to O(eps_q), confirming the theorem attributes the failure to NON-SMOOTHNESS of the quantizer.
